'''Ofelia Teresa Alas''' (born 4 June 1943) is Brazilian mathematician and professor emeritus at the [[Institute of Mathematics and Statistics, University of São Paulo]]. She served as its vice-dean in the years from 1990 to 1994, under [[Pedro Alberto Morettin]]'s warrant. Alas is a researcher in the fields of [[topology]] and [[set theory]]. She is notable for being the second Brazilian woman to obtain a PhD in mathematics from a Brazilian institution.

==Early life==
Ofelia Alas was born in [[São Paulo]], Brazil on 4 June 1943,<ref name=":0" /> daughter of a engineer and a piano teacher. Since childhood, she had showed interest in mathematics.

== Career ==
Alas obteined a bachelor's and licence degree in mathematics in 1964 from the [[University of São Paulo]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2023-09-01 |title=Galeria de Diretores: Ofélia Teresa Alas |url=https://www.ime.usp.br/historia/galeria-de-diretores-e-vice-diretores/ofelia-teresa-alas/ |access-date=2025-08-07 |website=IME-USP |language=pt-BR |archive-date=14 August 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250814141001/https://www.ime.usp.br/historia/galeria-de-diretores-e-vice-diretores/ofelia-teresa-alas/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last=Machado |first=Suélen Rita Andrade |date=2023-12-31 |title=O PROTAGONISMO FEMININO NO DESENVOLVIMENTO DA MATEMÁTICA NO BRASIL |url=https://www.sbembrasil.org.br/periodicos/index.php/rceem/article/view/3725 |journal=Revista Cearense de Educação Matemática |volume=2 |issue=5 |pages=1–20 |doi=10.56938/rceem.v2i5.3725 |issn=2764-8311 |doi-access=free |archive-date=3 May 2025 |access-date=7 August 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250503203844/https://www.sbembrasil.org.br/periodicos/index.php/rceem/article/view/3725 |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 1965, she became the only woman to receive a fellowship to develop activities in Instituto de Pesquisas Matemáticas at USP.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bádue |first=Gabriel Soares |date=September 2018 |title=A INSTITUCIONALIZAÇÃO DA MATEMÁTICA APLICADA NA ESCOLA POLITÉCNICA DA UNIVERSIDADE DE SÃO PAULO (1940 – 1970) |url=https://repositorio.ufba.br/bitstream/ri/28049/1/GSB_Tese_vf.pdf |access-date=2025-08-07 |website=ufba |archive-date=1 June 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250601064553/https://repositorio.ufba.br/bitstream/ri/28049/1/GSB_Tese_vf.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref> 

She finished her master's degree in 1967 with the thesis ''Seis proposições equivalentes ao Teorema de Zermelo'' and her PhD in 1968, with the thesis ''Sobre uma Extensão do Conceito de Compacidade e suas Aplicações'', both supervised by [[Edison Farah]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Moraes |first=Carlos Roberto de |date=2007 |title=Uma história da lógica no Brasil |url=https://repositorio.unesp.br/server/api/core/bitstreams/28bd2b1b-3d1e-4ac2-830b-67d364d81de0/content |access-date=2025-08-07 |website=Universidade Estadual Paulista |language=pt-br |archive-date=16 November 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241116021646/https://repositorio.unesp.br/server/api/core/bitstreams/28bd2b1b-3d1e-4ac2-830b-67d364d81de0/content |url-status=live }}</ref> She became the second Brazilian woman to earn a mathematical doctoral's title from a Brazilian institution.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Silva |first=Clóvis Pereira da |url=https://accefyn.com/PubliAcad/Clovis/Clovispdf/8.pdf |title=A Matemática No Brasil - Uma História de seu Desenvolvimento: O desenvolvimento da Matemática no Brasil, da década de 1930 à década de 1980 |date= |language=pt-br |access-date=2025-08-08}}</ref><ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

In these programs, Ofelia Alas noted that there were very few women present.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

In 1968, Alas worked as an assistent professor at the [[University of São Paulo]], but resigned for personal reasons. She've done researchers in France and Argentina. In 1975, she was rehired as temporary professor and, one year later, she was hired as a full time. Alas became the first associate woman professor. The second woman to obtain this title was Mary Lilian Lourenço, in 2000.<ref name=":1" />

Between 1981 and 1983, she worked in a post-doc at the [[University of Toronto]].<ref name=":2">Cavalari, M.F. (2013). «Mulheres Pioneiras na Matemática no Brasil». Revista do Professor de Matemática. '''30''': 5-9</ref>

In 1990, Ofelia Alas was approved as full professor at the Institute of Mathematics and Statistics and retired in 1994, but continues to contribute as senior. Between 1990 and 1994, she served as vice-dean of IME-USP, working alongside dean Pedro Alberto Morettin.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />  

She is a member of the [[Brazilian Mathematical Society]], [[American Mathematical Society]] and the [[Academia de Ciências do Estado de São Paulo]].<ref name=":2" />

== Research ==
Alas is a researcher in topology and set theory's fields, with enphasis in [[collectionwise normal space]].<ref name=":0" />

Here is a small collection of Ofelia's works.

* 1964: ''On gauss spaces.''<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Alas |first=O. T. |date=1969 |title=On gauss spaces |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/BF02410785 |journal=Annali di Matematica Pura ed Applicata |language=en |volume=82 |issue=1 |pages=25–33 |doi=10.1007/BF02410785 |issn=0373-3114}}</ref>
* 1970: ''Topological groups and the generalized continuum hypothesis.''<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Alas |first=Ofelia Teresa |date=1970-01-01 |title=Topological groups and the generalized continuum hypothesis |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/proceedings-of-the-japan-academy-series-a-mathematical-sciences/volume-46/issue-7.S1/Topological-groups-and-the-generalized-continuum-hypothesis/10.3792/pja/1195526589.full |journal=Proceedings of the Japan Academy, Series A, Mathematical Sciences |volume=46 |issue=7.S1 |doi=10.3792/pja/1195526589 |issn=0386-2194 |archive-date=8 October 2024 |access-date=7 August 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241008120625/https://projecteuclid.org/journals/proceedings-of-the-japan-academy-series-a-mathematical-sciences/volume-46/issue-7.S1/Topological-groups-and-the-generalized-continuum-hypothesis/10.3792/pja/1195526589.full |url-status=live }}</ref>
* 1970: ''Une proposition équivalente au théorème de Zermelo.''<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Alas |first=Ofelia Teresa |date=1970-01-01 |title=Une proposition équivalente au théorème de Zermelo |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/proceedings-of-the-japan-academy-series-a-mathematical-sciences/volume-46/issue-5/Une-proposition-%c3%a9quivalente-au-th%c3%a9or%c3%a8me-de-Zermelo/10.3792/pja/1195520303.full |journal=Proceedings of the Japan Academy, Series A, Mathematical Sciences |volume=46 |issue=5 |doi=10.3792/pja/1195520303 |issn=0386-2194 |archive-date=18 November 2024 |access-date=7 August 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241118060514/https://projecteuclid.org/journals/proceedings-of-the-japan-academy-series-a-mathematical-sciences/volume-46/issue-5/Une-proposition-%C3%A9quivalente-au-th%C3%A9or%C3%A8me-de-Zermelo/10.3792/pja/1195520303.full |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Alas is a mother of two.<ref name=":1" />
